title: CmdPal: CmdPal shortcuts can fire twice

status.label: Fix in progress
status.detail: PR #50427 implements the HC_ACTION-only keyboard-hook guard in the affected Command Palette listener.

summary: Command Palette's local keyboard listener can raise one shortcut twice because it processes every nonnegative hook code instead of restricting event dispatch to HC_ACTION.
next_action: Track and validate PR #50427 rather than starting a duplicate implementation.

judgment.rationale: The exact hook-contract defect is now covered by linked upstream PR #50427, which changes LocalKeyboardListener to process HC_ACTION notifications only.
evidence: LocalKeyboardListener installs a thread-local WH_KEYBOARD hook with SetWindowsHookEx.
KeyEventHook currently invokes a key event whenever nCode is nonnegative and the lParam transition bit indicates key-down.
The WH_KEYBOARD callback contract uses HC_ACTION for a message removed from the queue and HC_NOREMOVE for a peek that remains queued.
Processing HC_NOREMOVE permits the same queued key to be reported again when it is later removed as HC_ACTION.
MainWindow and SettingsWindow both consume LocalKeyboardListener.KeyPressed for navigation shortcuts, so duplicate dispatch can execute a command twice.
PR #50427 is linked as the closing pull request and changes LocalKeyboardListener.cs plus its native-method declarations to implement the HC_ACTION filter.
judgment.recommended_action: Review and validate PR #50427; do not start a competing fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open upstream PR #50427 directly implements the reported HC_ACTION-only handling in LocalKeyboardListener.

issue_context.summary: The report describes a Windows hook semantics bug rather than an environment-specific shortcut conflict: Command Palette consumes keyboard notifications that are not ready for processing.
known_information: The report names LocalKeyboardListener and specifically identifies HC_NOREMOVE processing.
The current implementation installs a WH_KEYBOARD hook for the current UI thread.
The callback condition is nCode >= 0 combined with a key-down transition check.
MainWindow uses the listener for GoBack, XButton1, and Alt+Left navigation.
SettingsWindow uses the same listener for GoBack.
Linked PR #50427 changes the listener to process only HC_ACTION and closes this issue.
inferences: A message loop or control that peeks before removing a keyboard message can cause the same physical key to produce two KeyPressed notifications.
Restricting dispatch to HC_ACTION should remove the duplicate without changing valid shortcut behavior.
issue_context.analysis: The hook code is the decisive signal. HC_NOREMOVE is informational and the message remains queued, so invoking application behavior from it violates the callback contract. PR #50427 now owns the narrow correction; dashboard work should track that implementation instead of offering a parallel design action.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, labels, assignee, and automated triage comment.
Reviewed Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Helpers/LocalKeyboardListener.cs and confirmed the broad nCode condition.
Reviewed MainWindow and SettingsWindow subscribers to identify the user-visible duplicate navigation paths.
Reviewed file history: the condition originates from the initial local keyboard listener implementation and has not received a hook-code correctness fix.
Confirmed Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.UnitTests exists as the nearest focused test project.
Inspected linked PR #50427 and confirmed its two-file scope directly targets the reported listener condition.

design.root_cause: The WH_KEYBOARD hook callback dispatches application events for HC_NOREMOVE because it treats all nonnegative nCode values as actionable. HC_NOREMOVE reports a peeked message that remains in the queue, so the later HC_ACTION notification can dispatch the same shortcut a second time.
evidence: The callback invokes InvokeKeyDown directly from that condition.
Both Command Palette windows attach behavior-changing subscribers to KeyPressed.

affected_files.purpose: Defines the WH_KEYBOARD callback and decides whether to raise KeyPressed.
New focused regression coverage for hook-code and transition filtering.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: KeyEventHook raises KeyPressed for any nonnegative hook code when the transition-state bit indicates key-down, including HC_NOREMOVE.
implementation_steps.change: Require the hook code to equal HC_ACTION before reading the key payload and raising KeyPressed. Keep CallNextHookEx unconditional so ignored notifications continue through the hook chain.
edge_cases: Negative nCode values must be forwarded without inspecting the payload.
HC_NOREMOVE must be forwarded without raising KeyPressed.
Key-up and autorepeat transition semantics should remain governed by the existing lParam bit check.
Exceptions from subscribers must remain logged without breaking the hook chain.
tests: HC_ACTION plus a key-down lParam returns true.
HC_NOREMOVE plus the same key-down lParam returns false.
HC_ACTION plus a previous-key-down transition returns false.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The UI unit-test project has no regression test for the Windows hook callback contract.
implementation_steps.change: Add data-driven tests around the extracted internal predicate. If internals are not currently visible to the test assembly, add the project-standard InternalsVisibleTo declaration rather than exercising a real global hook.
edge_cases: Do not install a real keyboard hook in unit tests.
Use the generated Windows constants or a named local constant instead of unexplained numeric values in production code.
Keep the test independent of keyboard layout and current modifier state.
tests: Run the new data-driven cases on x64.
Confirm the existing Command Palette UI unit tests remain green.

verify: Build Microsoft.CmdPal.UI with the repository's existing architecture configuration.
Launch Command Palette and verify GoBack, XButton1, and Alt+Left execute once per physical input.
Confirm ignored hook notifications still reach CallNextHookEx.
risks: A generated PInvoke constant may use a different symbol shape than PInvoke.HC_ACTION; use the repository's available Windows constant or a documented named constant.
Changing callback filtering affects every LocalKeyboardListener subscriber, but only removes non-actionable notifications.
A test-only visibility change may be required if the predicate remains internal.
alternatives: Debounce duplicate KeyPressed events in each subscriber. Rejected because it hides the hook-contract violation, adds timing behavior, and duplicates logic.
Track the last virtual key and suppress repeats. Rejected because legitimate autorepeat and distinct repeated presses would become ambiguous.

verify: Confirm one KeyPressed event is raised for one actionable keyboard message.
Confirm HC_NOREMOVE and negative hook codes are forwarded without invoking Command Palette behavior.
